Query Supabase as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__supabase.R
oauth_db_supabase_api.Rd

Read Supabase tables or call database functions using each visitor's account. The Data API exposes PostgreSQL data over HTTPS, so no database driver is needed. Database grants and row-level security policies control which records the user can read or change.

Usage

oauth_db_supabase_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  api_key,
  schema = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 30,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

url

HTTPS Supabase project base URL, without /rest/v1 or /auth/v1. Custom domains and reverse proxy paths are supported.

api_key

Project publishable key (sb_publishable_...) or legacy anon JWT. Secret and service_role keys are rejected.

schema

Exposed PostgreSQL schema, or NULL for the server default.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds for one request, including its refresh retry.

ca_bundle

Optional path to a trusted CA certificate bundle.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A client object with the same select(), rpc(), and request() methods as oauth_db_postgrest_api(). select() returns a data frame; rpc() and request() return the parsed JSON value, or an httr2 response with raw = TRUE.

Details

Create the client inside server() and call its methods from render or reactive expressions. Use oauth_db_supabase_client() for project sign-in, or an authorization from a third-party provider the project trusts.

The project key identifies the application; the visitor's token supplies their identity. OAuth scopes don't grant table access, so configure database grants and row-level security policies too. This client uses the Data API; use a separate helper for a direct SQL connection.

Requests use a current token and discard results after sign-out or account changes. GET and HEAD can refresh and retry once after HTTP 401; writes and POST function calls don't retry automatically. HTTPS is required, including for self-hosted projects.

See also

oauth_db_supabase_client(), oauth_db_postgrest_api(). vignette("supabase", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has setup instructions and a complete Shiny app.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
supabase <- oauth_db_supabase_api(auth$connection,
  url = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SUPABASE_URL"),
  api_key = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SUPABASE_KEY"))
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  supabase$select("orders", order = "id.asc", limit = 20L)
})
} # }
